ENGLISH LANGUAGE — MOCK EXAM #12
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
TIME ALLOWED: 2 hours
TOTAL MARKS: 80
EXAM BODY: KPSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Intensive Reading.

3. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. blue
   B. happiness
   C. quickly
   D. run

4. When practising Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 2.4.1 Creative Writing.

5. When practising Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in uses 2.3.1 Word Classes: Nouns.

6. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

7. When practising Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

8. When practising Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 1.1.1 Pronunciation and Vocabulary.

9. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Functional writing.

10. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. goes
   D. went

11. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading.

12. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. A person, place, thing, or idea
   C. Only a describing word
   D. Only an action

13. When practising Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners.

14. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. One main idea with supporting sentences
   B. No full stops
   C. Many unrelated topics with no link
   D. Only one word repeated

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
15. In three clear sentences, explain Pronunciation and Vocabulary and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 13.2.1 Extensive Reading: Independent Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

17. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 13.3.1 Word Class: Prepositions and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

21. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 1.2.1 Extensive Reading and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

22. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in use 1.3.1 Word Classes: Determiners and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
